theory.intro: When an expression has several operations, everyone agrees to work them out in a fixed order so the answer is the same.
facts: Do **brackets** first, then **multiplication and division** (left to right), then **addition and subtraction** (left to right).
Multiplication and division have **equal** priority — work left to right.
Without the agreed order, the same expression could give different answers.
steps: Do all $\times$ and $\div$ from left to right.
Do all $+$ and $-$ from left to right.

workedExamples.question_text:
Evaluate each expression. Explain which operation you do first.
(a) $51-7 \times 6+8$
(b) $31-12+5$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Multiply before subtracting or adding.
$51-7 \times 6+8$
$=51-42+8$
$=9+8$
$=17$
(b) Subtraction and addition have equal priority, so work from left to right.
$31-12+5$
$=19+5$
$=24$

workedExamples.question_text: Evaluate $84 \div 7 \times 3+11$. Explain why you divide before multiplying.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Division and multiplication have equal priority. Read them from left to right, so divide $84$ by $7$ first.
$84 \div 7 \times 3+11$
$=12 \times 3+11$
$=36+11$
$=47$

workedExamples.question_text:
Evaluate both expressions. Explain how the brackets change the first operation.
(a) $5 \times (17-8)+14$
(b) $5 \times 17-8+14$
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Do the subtraction inside the brackets first.
$5 \times (17-8)+14$
$=5 \times 9+14$
$=45+14$
$=59$
(b) There are no brackets, so multiply before subtracting or adding.
$5 \times 17-8+14$
$=85-8+14$
$=77+14$
$=91$
The brackets make $17-8$ a group that is worked out before multiplying.

workedExamples.question_text:
A group buys $5$ tickets at $8$ dollars each and $3$ maps at $7$ dollars each.
Write a number sentence and find the total cost.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Multiply to find each cost, then add the two costs.
$5 \times 8+3 \times 7$
$=40+3 \times 7$
$=40+21$
$=61$
The total cost is $61$ dollars.

mastery.question_text:
Four coaches each carry $12$ balls, and a store room has another $17$ balls.
Evaluate $4 \times 12+17$ to find the total.

A club has $90$ badges in its supply.
It will award $48$ badges equally among $6$ teams.
One team collects its share.
Evaluate $90-48 \div 6$ to find how many badges remain in the supply.
